core.title: Structure every acceptance as Given/When/Then
core.given: You are authoring or revising an acceptance.
core.when: You write a new acceptance or change any of its sections (given, when or then — one is enough).
core.then: Give the acceptance a required `when` declaring the single harness-specific trigger and a required `then` that is an array of assertions, with `given` declaring only the required preconditions.
prefer: Express required preconditions in `given` using the stack's listed precondition fields, and include a precondition only when the scenario needs it.
Shape `when` in the trigger form the acceptance's harness prescribes (per the stack's acceptance schema).
Use only the stack's allowed assertion kinds in `then`.
avoid: More than one trigger in `when`, or a trigger not expressed in the trigger form its harness prescribes.
Putting into `given` preconditions the scenario does not require.
`then` that is not an array, or assertions using a kind outside the stack's allowed list.
core.why: A uniform, minimal Given/When/Then shape lets each acceptance be executed by its harness and checked mechanically: one trigger keeps the scenario unambiguous, typed assertions keep outcomes verifiable.
evidence: Each acceptance has a `when` that declares exactly one trigger, expressed in the trigger form its harness prescribes.
Each acceptance has a `then` that is an array of assertions, each using a kind from the stack's allowed list.

`given` declares only preconditions the scenario requires (the stack's listed precondition fields are a listed vocabulary, not an exclusive allow-list, so a required precondition is not rejected merely for its field name).
verification: The check is structural: it verifies that `when` is present and declares exactly one trigger in the form the acceptance's harness prescribes (the per-harness trigger forms come from the stack's acceptance schema, via the profile), and that `then` is present, is an array, and that every assertion's kind is within the stack's allowed assertion-kind list.

The precondition-field list is not an exclusive allow-list: a precondition is not rejected merely because its field name is not listed; the only constraint stated for `given` is that it declares preconditions the scenario requires.

Whether a precondition is actually required by the scenario is not mechanically derivable; the check does not cover the required-ness of a precondition, only the structural shape of `when` and `then`.

fires: The planner writes a new acceptance
The planner revises any part of an existing acceptance, even a single section (only given, only when, or only then)
The planner adds or changes an assertion in an acceptance's then
doesNotFire: Editing only a plan artifact or plan narrative that contains no acceptance
The coder implements production code that an acceptance already describes
Editing docs that merely mention acceptances without defining one

profileRequirements.meaning: The precondition fields the stack's acceptance schema lists for an acceptance's `given` section; a listed vocabulary, not an exclusive allow-list.
The trigger form an acceptance's `when` must take for each harness kind the stack's acceptance schema defines.
profileRequirements.bunValue: http → method/path; unit → target; event → topic; ws/e2e → interactions

profileRequirements.meaning: The exclusive allow-list of assertion kinds a `then` assertion may use in the stack's acceptance schema.
profileRequirements.bunValue: status, body, headers, error, event_published, state_changed, metric

bunOnly.text: Source example (http when): when.http: {method: POST, path: /api/users, body: {name: John}}
bunOnly.reason: Concrete worked example of the stack's acceptance schema; the neutral core refers only to the harness-prescribed trigger form via the profile, and bun.json remains the reference example.

bunOnly.text: Source example (unit when): when.unit: {target: UserService.createUser, args: {userData: {name: John}}}
bunOnly.reason: Concrete worked example naming a production symbol; no stack-neutral equivalent beyond the profile's unit trigger form.

bunOnly.text: Source example (then): then: [{kind: status, expect: 200}, {kind: error, expect: {code: USER_EXISTS}}]
bunOnly.reason: Concrete worked example of typed assertions; the neutral core keeps only the array-of-allowed-kind-assertions obligation.

neutralityNotes: The Given/When/Then section names themselves are kept in the core: they are the convention's own subject (the acceptance DSL), not stack machinery. What is stack-specific is the acceptance-schema data behind the obligation: the listed precondition fields, the per-harness trigger forms, and the assertion-kind allow-list. Vocabulary v2 has no keys for these, so three idiom keys are proposed and referenced from profileRequirements; instantiated with the Bun values they reproduce bun.json exactly (the allow-list stays exclusive for assertion kinds, non-exclusive for given fields). The 'wagon' term in the Bun doesNotFire ('Editing only a wagon or plan narrative that contains no acceptance') is a stack layout concept and was generalized to 'plan artifact or plan narrative'; behavior is unchanged because both formulations cover edits that touch no acceptance. The three source examples in verifier_detail are concrete data examples with no neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly, since bun.json is delivered as the worked reference example.
